deep.reconstruction:
Context: E283 lists, for each prime P = 4n+1, all a with P | a^2+1, so that a^2+1 can later be tested for primality. Euler first writes P = p^2 + q^2 (p > q). He runs the Euclidean algorithm on (p, q) and forms the continued-fraction convergents of p/q. If r/s is the penultimate convergent, he sets a = r p + s q, and then every solution is a = mP ± a.

Why it works: r q - s p = ±1. Hence a q - p = s(p^2 + q^2) = sP (up to sign handling), so a ≡ p q^{-1} (mod P). From p^2 ≡ -q^2 it follows that a^2 ≡ -1. On the previous page Euler checks this for 1709 = 22^2 + 35^2, getting a = 390; indeed 390^2 + 1 = 89·1709.

This page gives three special cases.
- Coroll. 1: P = p^2 + 1, so q = 1. There is a single quotient p and the convergents are 1/0, p/1. So a = 1·p + 0·1 = p and a = m(4n+1) ± p. This is trivially right, since p^2 + 1 = P.
- Coroll. 2: P = p^2 + (p-1)^2, so q = p-1. The quotients are 1 and p-1, the convergents 1/0, 1/1, p/(p-1). So a = 1·p + 1·(p-1) = 2p-1, and a = Pm ± (2p-1). Check: (2p-1)^2 + 1 = 4p^2 - 4p + 2 = 2P.
- Coroll. 3: the prime 2 = 1 + 1 is not of the form 4n+1, but formally p = q = 1. Coroll. 1 gives a = 1, so a = 2m ± 1. This is the obvious fact that odd squares plus 1 are even.

These cases feed the table on the next page.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. Coroll. 3 applies a rule stated for 4n+1 primes to P = 2; Euler acknowledges this and it is harmless. On the next page the table entry '2 = 1^2+2^2' should read 1^2+1^2 (a misprint or transcription slip, not on this page).

ideas.what: Square root of -1 mod a prime P = p^2+q^2 obtained as p·q^{-1} mod P, with the inverse computed by continued-fraction convergents (a = r p + s q).
ideas.modern_name: Computing sqrt(-1) mod p from a two-square representation; extended Euclidean algorithm. This is the converse direction of the Hermite–Serret / Cornacchia algorithm.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / Lagrange–Gauss era. The converse direction (from sqrt(-1) to p^2+q^2) is credited to Hermite and Serret (1848) and Cornacchia (1908).

ideas.what: Closed forms a = p for P = p^2+1 and a = 2p-1 for P = p^2+(p-1)^2.
ideas.modern_name: Trivial explicit square roots of -1 for special primes

ideas.what: Extension of the rule to the prime 2.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of correct but elementary special cases of Euler's continued-fraction recipe for sqrt(-1) mod P. The recipe itself is in E283 and amounts to inverting q mod P; nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In Coroll. 1 the printed text reads 'a=1.p+0.1=p' (with the '=' poorly printed); the transcription's 'a=1.p+0.1=p' is correct.
In Coroll. 1 the quotient p is printed above the fractions 1/0, p/1, matching the transcription.
